chapter: Primate Taxonomy and Comparative Anatomy

A sagittal crest develops in large-jawed male primates (e.g., gorilla, Paranthropus boisei) to anchor massive temporalis masticatory muscles.

chapter: Early Hominid Evolution and Australopithecines
questionText: Taphonomic research by C. K. Brain at Swartkrans cave proved that Australopithecines were not bloodthirsty hunters, but rather:

options.text: Herbivores that lived entirely underwater
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option 'Herbivores that lived entirely underwater'. Conflates core domain concepts or theories with adjacent terminology.

options.text: The hunted prey of extinct carnivores (such as the false sabertooth leopard Megantereon)
options.mistakeAnalysis: Correct answer. Accurately explains C. K. Brain Taphonomic Reinterpretation.

options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option 'Aliens from outer space'. Attributes historical facts, dates, authors, or mechanisms to an incorrect entity.

options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option 'Masters of iron metallurgy'. Adopts an over-generalized or inaccurate interpretation contradictory to syllabus facts.

Brain matched puncture marks on the skull of a juvenile hominin with the canine teeth of a leopard, proving early hominins were hunted prey rather than apex hunters.
Hence, Option B is correct.

chapter: Evolution of Genus Homo: Homo habilis and Homo erectus

Isolated on island Flores, H. floresiensis underwent insular dwarfism, adapting to limited endemic resources while maintaining Oldowan stone technology.

chapter: Neanderthals and Anatomically Modern Homo sapiens
questionText: In human evolutionary genetics, 'Mitochondrial Eve' refers to:

options.text: A fossil skeleton found in a museum

options.mistakeAnalysis: Correct answer. Accurately explains Mitochondrial Eve Concept.

options.text: A female chimpanzee
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option 'A female chimpanzee'. Adopts an over-generalized or inaccurate interpretation contradictory to syllabus facts.

detailedSolution:
Mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA) is inherited strictly through maternal lines; coalescent analysis traces all modern human mtDNA back to a female in Africa ~150–200 ka.
Hence, Option C is correct.

chapter: Human Genetics and Mendelian Inheritance in Man
questionText: Can a human father transmit an X-linked recessive genetic disease (e.g., Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy) directly to his biological son?

options.text: Yes, fathers give both X and Y to sons
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option 'Yes, fathers give both X and Y to sons'. Conflates core domain concepts or theories with adjacent terminology.

options.text: No, because a father contributes his Y chromosome, not his X chromosome, to his male offspring
options.mistakeAnalysis: Correct answer. Accurately explains Father to Son X-Chromosome Transmission.

options.text: Yes, X chromosomes jump through the air
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option 'Yes, X chromosomes jump through the air'. Attributes historical facts, dates, authors, or mechanisms to an incorrect entity.

options.text: Only if the father is blood group AB
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option 'Only if the father is blood group AB'. Adopts an over-generalized or inaccurate interpretation contradictory to syllabus facts.

detailedSolution:
Males inherit their single X chromosome exclusively from their mother and the Y chromosome from their father; father-to-son X-transmission is genetically impossible.
Hence, Option B is correct.

chapter: Genetic Polymorphisms and Inborn Errors of Metabolism

options.text: Complete starvation
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option 'Complete starvation'. Adopts an over-generalized or inaccurate interpretation contradictory to syllabus facts.

detailedSolution:
Restricting dietary phenylalanine while supplying essential tyrosine allows normal cerebral myelination and completely normal cognitive development.
Hence, Option C is correct.

chapter: Dermatoglyphics and Anthropometric Indices

Nasal index grades from narrow/leptorrhine (cold/dry adapted) to medium/mesorrhine to broad/platyrrhine (warm/humid tropical adapted).
Hence, Option B is correct.

chapter: Human Variation and Biological Concept of Race
questionText: Richard Lewontin's landmark 1972 study 'The Apportionment of Human Diversity' demonstrated through blood protein polymorphisms that:

options.text: 85.4% of total human genetic diversity exists WITHIN any single local population, and only ~6% to 10% accounts for classical 'racial' differences
options.mistakeAnalysis: Correct answer. Accurately explains Lewontin's 1972 Genetic Diversity Study.

options.text: Each race has its own unique 10,000 genes
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option 'Each race has its own unique 10,000 genes'. Conflates core domain concepts or theories with adjacent terminology.

options.text: Human races are completely different biological species
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option 'Human races are completely different biological species'. Attributes historical facts, dates, authors, or mechanisms to an incorrect entity.

options.text: Human genes never cross continents
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option 'Human genes never cross continents'. Adopts an over-generalized or inaccurate interpretation contradictory to syllabus facts.

detailedSolution:
Lewontin proved that human racial categories have negligible genetic taxonomic significance: two random individuals from the same village differ genetically almost as much as two people from different continents.
Hence, Option A is correct.

chapter: Ecological Anthropology and Environmental Adaptations
questionText: The hypoxia-pathway transcription factor gene 'EPAS1', present in >87% of high-altitude Tibetans, prevents which pathological maladaptation common in lowlanders?

options.text: Chronic Mountain Sickness (Monge's disease) caused by excessive, thick, life-threatening polycythemia (hyper-viscous blood)

options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option 'Blindness in sunlight'. Conflates core domain concepts or theories with adjacent terminology.

EPAS1 down-regulates excessive hemoglobin overproduction, allowing Tibetans to deliver oxygen efficiently via elevated blood flow without lethal blood sludging.
Hence, Option A is correct.

chapter: Concept of Culture and Society

detailedSolution:
Ideal culture consists of the formal values, virtues, and rules people profess to uphold; real culture consists of the actual empirical behaviors enacted in everyday reality.
Hence, Option B is correct.

chapter: Marriage: Forms, Rules and Tribal Mate Acquisition

Cross-cousins are offspring of opposite-sex siblings (mother's brother or father's sister), widely preferred as ideal marriage partners in many tribal and South Indian groups.

chapter: Family: Types, Functions and Matrilineal Systems

The Hindu joint family is defined by commensality (common kitchen), common residence, joint property ownership (coparcenary), shared worship, and Karta's authority.

Agnates are relatives traced exclusively through males; Uterines are relatives traced exclusively through females.

Couvade publicly cements the social tie of paternity, asserting the husband's moral claims over the child and expressing psychological sympathy with the mother.

chapter: Economic Anthropology: Primitive Economy and Exchange
questionText: In the Himalayas and arid zones, tribal pastoralists (such as the Bakarwals, Gaddis, and Gujjars) practice 'Transhumance', which is defined as:

options.text: Permanent year-round confinement of animals in closed industrial feedlots
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option 'Permanent year-round confinement of animals in closed industrial feedlots'. Conflates core domain concepts or theories with adjacent terminology.

options.text: The random wandering of livestock with no human guidance
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option 'The random wandering of livestock with no human guidance'. Attributes historical facts, dates, authors, or mechanisms to an incorrect entity.

options.mistakeAnalysis: Correct answer. Accurately explains Pastoral Nomadism and Transhumance.

options.text: The slaughter of all herds every autumn
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option 'The slaughter of all herds every autumn'. Adopts an over-generalized or inaccurate interpretation contradictory to syllabus facts.

detailedSolution:
Transhumance is vertical seasonal pastoral movement: ascending to lush alpine bugyals/pastures in summer and descending to warmer lowlands during snowbound winters.
Hence, Option C is correct.

chapter: Political Anthropology: Law, Order and Social Control
questionText: In tribal anthropology, a 'Blood Feud' is an institutionalized state of mutual hostility between two lineages triggered by homicide, which ends when:

options.text: The United Nations sends peacekeeping troops
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option 'The United Nations sends peacekeeping troops'. Adopts an over-generalized or inaccurate interpretation contradictory to syllabus facts.

detailedSolution:
A blood feud is not random murder; it is a structured, regulated conflict where customary law permits vengeance or reconciliation via cattle/wealth indemnity.
Hence, Option C is correct.

Mana is potent impersonal sacred force; things or individuals infused with high mana become Taboo (prohibited, untouchable) to prevent dangerous supernatural backlash.

detailedSolution:
Anuloma (with the grain / hypergamy) allows a higher varna male to marry a lower varna female; Pratiloma (against the grain / hypogamy) is strictly condemned.
Hence, Option A is correct.

Emic captures native meanings, concepts, and values ('the insider's point of view'); Etic applies objective, external scientific categories to analyze social reality.

African pluvials were named after East African river basins: Kageran (oldest), Kamasian, Kanjeran, and Gamblian (youngest pluvial).

Fossil tooth enamel is exceptionally crystalline; ESR measures accumulated trapped charges in enamel hydroxyapatite, dating hominid teeth from 50 ka to over 2 Ma.

chapter: Evolution of Genus Homo: Homo habilis and Homo erectus
topic: Liang Bua Cave Location and Nickname
questionText:
Read the following case study on the Discovery of Homo floresiensis ('The Hobbit') on the Island of Flores, and answer the questions that follow:

In September 2003, a joint Australian-Indonesian archaeological team led by Michael Morwood and Raden Soejono made a stunning discovery in the limestone cave of Liang Bua on the isolated Indonesian island of Flores. Excavating deep deposits, they unearthed a remarkably preserved, nearly complete adult hominin skeleton (cataloged as LB1), nicknamed 'The Hobbit'. Described in 'Nature' in 2004 by Peter Brown, the specimen represented an adult female standing just 1.06 meters (3 feet 6 inches) tall and weighing approximately 25–30 kilograms, with a cranial brain volume of merely 417 to 426 cc—smaller than an average chimpanzee. Yet associated archaeological layers contained sophisticated stone tools, evidence of controlled fire, and butchered bones of dwarf Stegodon (an extinct elephant relative). Radiocarbon and luminescence dating subsequently established that Homo floresiensis occupied Liang Bua from approximately 100,000 to 60,000 years ago. Evolutionary biologists explain this miniature human through 'Insular Dwarfism' (Foster's Island Rule): when large mammals become isolated on small oceanic islands with limited caloric food resources and an absence of apex mammalian predators, natural selection favors rapid body size reduction. Brain shape analyses demonstrated that despite its microcephalic brain size, floresiensis possessed derived cortical reorganization in the frontal lobe (Brodmann area 10) associated with complex planning and tool manufacture.

Question: The fossil hominin known as 'The Hobbit' (Homo floresiensis) was excavated from Liang Bua Cave on which isolated Indonesian island?

options.text: Java Island
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option 'Java Island'. Conflates core domain concepts or theories with adjacent terminology.

options.text: Flores Island
options.mistakeAnalysis: Correct answer. Accurately analyzes case evidence on Liang Bua Cave Location and Nickname.

options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option 'Sumatra Island'. Attributes historical facts, dates, authors, or mechanisms to an incorrect entity.

options.text: Borneo Island
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option 'Borneo Island'. Adopts an over-generalized or inaccurate interpretation contradictory to syllabus facts.

detailedSolution:

Hence, Option B is correct.

chapter: Political Anthropology: Law, Order and Social Control
questionText:
Read the following excerpt on E.E. Evans-Pritchard's Study of the Nuer Segmentary Lineage System and Blood Feud, and answer the questions that follow:

In his classic 1940 monograph 'The Nuer', British social anthropologist E.E. Evans-Pritchard analyzed how political order is maintained in an 'acephalous' (headless) tribal society lacking centralized government, kings, courts, or police. The pastoral Nuer of the South Sudan were organized on the principle of the 'Segmentary Lineage System'. Political units were defined not by fixed geographic boundaries, but by genealogical distance along agnatic lineages. The system operated on 'Complementary Opposition': opposing segments at a lower level of segmentation fight one another, but instantly fuse into a larger unified bloc when confronted by an outside rival. Evans-Pritchard summarized this structural dynamic through the famous proverb: 'I against my brother; I and my brother against my cousin; I, my brother, and my cousin against the stranger'.
